title: 1번 — 자연법 이론에 대한 이해
fullPassage: According to natural law theory, moral principles are not simply the result of human convention or social agreement, but are based on fundamental principles of nature, including human nature. The term "natural law" refers to a set of ethical and moral principles that are thought to be inherent in the natural world and applicable to all human beings. These principles are considered to be objective, universal, and immutable, and are often seen as a source of guidance for human behaviour. Natural law theorists believe that the natural world operates according to a set of rational principles, and that these principles can be discovered through human reason and observation. They argue that these principles provide a foundation for moral and legal systems, and that they are binding on all individuals, regardless of their cultural or social background. Critics of natural law theory argue that it relies too heavily on unprovable assumptions about the existence of a divine purpose, and that it fails to account for the diversity of moral beliefs and practices across cultures and historical periods.
